why: Quotes a table key: a key that is a Lua identifier and not a reserved word is written bare, any other as ["..."]. It is lua's jsKey (which the printing helpers list holds), and it carries the shared reserved-word list a provider may not hold itself (naming.ts LUA_RESERVED); ts/test/lua-table-keys.test.ts requires every lua component that writes a key to import it rather than define its own.

Quotes a Lua string literal (escapes backslash, quote and newlines), as jsQuote does for js; a provider-local quoter would be a second copy. JSON.stringify is not a substitute: its \uXXXX escapes are not Lua syntax.
